articles.title: Mali drone kills 13 civilians, activists say; army says it targeted militants
articles.description: Local human rights activists and a separatist group say Mali's military killed at least 13 civilians in a drone strike earlier this week near the Mauritania border. Mali has faced al-Qaida-linked militants and a Tuareg separatist rebellion for over a decade. The military claims it targeted terrorists hiding motorcycles. However, a local official says a Tuareg camp was bombed, killing civilians, including women and children. Human Rights Watch reports that abusive counterinsurgency operations often harm civilians. The Sahel region, where Mali is located, has become a hot spot for extremist violence in recent years.

articles.title: Country diary: A vial of water from the rivers, becks and springs of Yorkshire – but not without permission | Amy-Jane Beer
articles.description: Wharram and York, North Yorkshire: It’s the nervy few days before a ceremony that will honour our local waterways, and I have work to do I visit the source of the tiny stream called the Gypsey Race now and then, drawn by the everyday miracle of its water welling to catch sunlight like a plaything and alchemise it into colours and sparks. Today, though, is different, because I’ve come to ask for something. Something like permission, or approval maybe. I’ve been helping to organise a gathering of river advocates to co-draft a regional charter of river rights – making explicit our responsibilities towards them. We will be holding a ceremony to blend waters from across Yorkshire to make ink in which the charter will be written. I want to collect water from the Gypsey, but I also want some of its potent reputation. Its course is regarded as auspicious thanks to an extraordinary concentration of nearby prehistoric barrows, cursuses and henges, not to mention England’s tallest standing stone. Local folklore insists that its capricious flow holds the power of prophecy. Continue reading...
